sources.title: 八字真宗 (Bát Tự Chân Tông)

sources.note: Popular practice manual. Used only for tables (stem/branch relations, ngũ hổ/ngũ thử độn, 12 stages, luck start rule, khong vong). Its fortune-telling statements (injury, death, children) are deliberately NOT implemented.

sources.title: Tử Vi Hàm Số
sources.author: Nguyễn Phát Lộc (Sài Gòn, 1972)
sources.edition: PDF of a Word transcription (trantuliem.blogspot.com), 238 PDF pages; printed page = PDF page − 1
sources.locator: Quyển Nhì pp.83-233 (ý nghĩa 14 chính tinh và các phụ tinh)
sources.note: Cited 'HS p.N' with the printed page. Readings paraphrased; each rule's verbatim quote is checked against the PDF text layer (engine/tests/test_ham_so.py). The author compiles Thái Thứ Lang and others and says so; his own objections are kept as his.

sources.title: The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (A. E. Waite's text), as reissued in The Illustrated Key to the Tarot: The Veil of Divination
sources.author: A. E. Waite (text); reissued by L. W. de Laurence
sources.edition: Chicago, 1916 (Library of Congress copyright deposit 5 Dec 1916); LoC scan, archive.org illustratedkeyto01dela, 188 PDF pages, OCR text layer. Pagination is this issue's, NOT the 1911 Rider edition's: printed page = PDF page - 8 (checked on page images: PDF 101 = p. 93, PDF 155 = p. 147). Cited 'PKT (1916) tr. N'.
sources.locator: Part II pp. 40-82 (Trumps Major descriptions); Part III pp. 90-145 (Lesser Arcana, Divinatory Meanings), pp. 146-147 (Section 3, Greater Arcana divinatory meanings)
sources.note: Public domain: published in the United States in 1916 (before 1930); Waite's text first published 1910/1911 and Waite died in 1942. The reissue adds '(Nature)' after 'God' in places; those spans are not quoted. Used only for the Tarot readings (engine/data/tarot/pack_tarot_pkt.json, tools/build_tarot_pack.py); every quote is checked on its printed page. Left out on purpose: death, illness, pregnancy or childbirth, accidents, prison or crime, sexual conduct, legal or financial instructions, lines framed as a certain future event, and the whole of Section 4 'Some additional meanings' (pp. 148-151).
